question: Assume today is 2026-08-29. You know nothing published after this date. Estimate the total freight carried by Canadian railways in July 2026, in tonnes, as it will be first reported by Statistics Canada in its monthly Railway carloadings release (total traffic carried, Canada).

target.what: Total tonnage of freight carried by Canadian railways in Canada during July 2026, as first reported by Statistics Canada in its monthly Railway carloadings release under total traffic carried.
target.caveats: Working interpretation: all freight tonnage reported in Statistics Canada's total traffic carried series for Canada, July 2026, using the first release rather than later revisions. Important alternatives include revenue freight only, domestic-origin traffic only, carloads rather than tonnes, or CN/C

candidates.hypothesis: July total tonnes has a recurring seasonal structure and a recent trend; July values from earlier years plus the latest published 2025-2026 monthly values can anchor a baseline. Symbolically, T_Jul2026 is inferred from the July seasonal level and the recent year-over-year run-rate, adjusted for known shocks.
candidates.data_to_find: Statistics Canada monthly Railway carloadings total traffic carried in tonnes for July 2021-2025 and the latest available months before the cutoff; first-release versus revised values; total carloads and average tonnes per carload where available. Minimum evidence: a consistent monthly total-tonnage series through mid-2026 and release timing for July 2026.
search_hints: Statistics Canada railway carloadings total traffic carried tonnes July 2025
site:www150.statcan.gc.ca railway carloadings monthly total tonnage
Statistics Canada Table 23-10-0218 total traffic carried

candidates.hypothesis: CN and CPKC carry most Canadian rail freight and report carloads and revenue ton-miles. Their Canadian traffic plus an allowance for shortlines and other carriers can bridge to Canada total; revenue ton-miles divided by average length of haul gives tonnage, while carloads times average tonnes per carload gives a cross-check.
candidates.data_to_find: CN and CPKC monthly or quarterly operating metrics for July 2026 and Q2/Q3 2026 if published: carloads, revenue ton-miles, average length of haul, Canadian-origin share, and any monthly volume releases. Minimum evidence: July 2026 carloads or revenue ton-miles plus an average haul or tonnes-per-carload bridge and a company-to-Canada coverage share. Substitute: company press releases, investor presentations, or weekly traffic reports.

Prior-year July commodity tonnages plus current production, export, and harvest signals can estimate each component and reduce reliance on a single aggregate trend.

Minimum evidence: July 2025 commodity mix and at least directional July 2026 signals for the largest commodities.

candidates.data_to_find: Statistics Canada manufacturing shipments, wholesale and retail trade, merchandise exports by mode, GDP or industrial production indicators for July 2026; commodity prices; harvest estimates. Minimum evidence: at least one broad activity indicator and one export indicator for July 2026, plus historical relationship to rail tonnage.

candidates.hypothesis: July 2026 may include disruptions or calendar effects that shift tonnage from the seasonal baseline, such as wildfires, labour actions, port closures, track outages, tariffs, or harvest timing. Measurable duration and affected traffic can constrain the adjustment.

Minimum evidence: a dated event list with quantitative or corridor-level exposure.

candidates.hypothesis: Published 2026 Canadian rail-volume forecasts or company guidance, multiplied by July's historical share of annual tonnage, can provide a top-down constraint. This is weaker than direct history but useful for bounding the estimate.
candidates.data_to_find: Railway Association of Canada, Transport Canada, CN/CPKC guidance, or analyst forecasts for 2026 Canadian rail tonnage or carloads; historical July share of annual total. Minimum evidence: an annual 2026 volume forecast and a July seasonal share from a consistent series.

methods.rationale: Channel sum that rebuilds the intermodal leg from unit counts rather than from July 2024 intermodal tonnage: p30 units times the tonnes-per-unit implied by the two kept July 2024 points p55 and p31, times an assumed 2025-to-2026 unit growth. Keeping the ratio p55/p31 inside the formula is what makes this a genuine structural cross-check on m2's intermodal leg; the shared p59/a2 and p57/a4 legs mean the other two channels are not independent of m2. Failure modes: p30/p31 include intermodal units of all origins while p55 covers only shipments originating in Canada, which biases the implied payload slightly low and hence this intermodal leg downward; a shift toward empty repositioning would bias it further down.

assumptions.name: July 2026 versus July 2024 total freight carried factor
assumptions.rationale: p53 is the exact StatCan July 2024 total. p68 shows 2025 annual tonnage essentially flat against p69's 2024 total, p67 shows December 2025 slightly down year over year, while p6/p7 show 2026 year-to-date RTMs up 4% with carloads flat and p1/p2 show week 32 of 2026 positive. Net two years out is near flat with a slight positive tilt; the band covers a weaker coal/US-origin cycle or a stronger grain year, and deliberately does not embed the late-summer harvest strength in p40/p41.
assumptions.applies_when: StatCan's total-traffic-carried definition and coverage are unchanged between July 2024 and July 2026 and no major strike, wildfire or track outage hits July 2026.
assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence of a large July 2026 disruption, a definition change in total traffic carried, or a 2026 monthly print far from 30 Mt.

assumptions.name: July 2026 versus July 2024 non-intermodal tonnage factor
assumptions.rationale: p73 shows 2025 non-intermodal annual tonnage up only marginally on 2024, p70 shows December 2025 down slightly, and p13 shows metals and minerals roughly flat year to date, while p3/p5 show grain and fertilizers strongly positive and p5 notes coal is the one declining RTM commodity. Offsetting commodity moves per p61-p66 imply a near-flat non-intermodal aggregate.
assumptions.applies_when: The non-intermodal commodity mix and StatCan classification remain comparable between 2024 and 2026.
assumptions.falsified_by: Commodity-level evidence of a sharp 2026 fall in grain, potash, coal, iron ore or metals loadings relative to 2024.

assumptions.name: July 2026 versus July 2024 intermodal tonnage factor
assumptions.rationale: p74 shows 2025 intermodal tonnage at an all-time high, up 7.4% on 2024, and p55/p56 show July 2024 was already up sharply; p30 versus p31 shows July unit counts rising further in 2025, and p1 reports intermodal carloads still increasing in week 32 of 2026. Two years of low-single-digit compounding supports a factor near this value; the band admits a tariff or port-driven stall.
assumptions.applies_when: Containerized traffic keeps growing at roughly the 2025-2026 pace and port/terminal throughput is not disrupted.
assumptions.falsified_by: Falling intermodal unit counts in mid-2026, a port labour disruption, or evidence that 2026 intermodal volumes fell below 2025.

assumptions.name: July 2026 versus July 2024 US-origin tonnage factor
assumptions.rationale: p57 gives the July 2024 US-origin base. p75 shows 2025 annual US-origin tonnage down 13.3% and the lowest since 2020, p72 shows December 2025 down 7.4% on an eleventh consecutive decline, and p76-p80 show the share falling from 12.0% in 2023-24 to 10.6% in Q3 2025 and 10.0% in Q4 2025. With the total near flat, a share fall of that size requires a two-year factor clearly below 1.
assumptions.applies_when: US rail-connection volumes remain on the 2025-early 2026 downward trajectory through July 2026.
assumptions.falsified_by: A rebound in US-origin traffic, or a Q3 2026 share back above roughly 11.5%.

assumptions.name: 2026 versus 2025 annual-level factor applied to the July share of annual tonnage
assumptions.rationale: p68/p69 show the 2025 annual total essentially flat versus 2024, while p6/p7 show 2026 year-to-date RTMs up 4% with carloads flat and p1/p2 show week 32 positive. A near-flat 2026 annual level with a slight positive tilt is the central case; the band admits weakening or acceleration. This factor adjusts only the 2025-to-2026 gap, because the July share itself is taken directly from kept points p53/p69 inside the formula.
assumptions.applies_when: The 2026 full-year level stays close to 2025 plus the observed year-to-date trend, and July 2026 seasonality resembles July 2024.
assumptions.falsified_by: A large divergence between 2026 year-to-date rail indicators and the eventual monthly outcome, or a major 2026 disruption.

assumptions.name: Average length of haul for the traffic represented by p38
assumptions.rationale: p82 gives CN's system-wide average haul of 742 miles, but p38 is Canadian Class 1 (CN plus CPKC) network-wide and is weighted toward long western bulk hauls (grain, potash, coal) and overseas movements through Canadian ports; p6/p7 show RTMs growing while carloads are flat, which means the average haul is rising. A Canada-weighted haul above the CN system average is therefore appropriate.
assumptions.applies_when: The commodity mix behind p38 keeps a Canada-weighted haul inside this band from Q3 2025 to July 2026.
assumptions.falsified_by: A published Canada-specific average length of haul outside this range for Class 1 traffic.

assumptions.name: July 2026 versus Q3 2025 monthly-average Class 1 tonnage factor
assumptions.rationale: p38 is a Q3 2025 quarter centred on August, and July is normally slightly below the quarter average, but p6/p7 show 2026 year-to-date RTMs up 4% versus 2025 and p1/p2 show week 32 of 2026 positive, so the net calendar-plus-trend effect is close to flat with upside risk.
assumptions.applies_when: The Q3 2025 quarter average is a serviceable base for a July 2026 month after applying the 2026 year-to-date trend.
assumptions.falsified_by: A sharp month-specific change in 2026 RTMs relative to the year-to-date pattern, or a July-specific disruption.

assumptions.name: Share of p38-derived Class 1 network-wide tonnage falling inside StatCan's Canada total traffic carried
assumptions.rationale: p38 is a Class 1 network-wide measure while the target is StatCan's Canada total; p90-p93 show CN's Canadian domestic business is only 17% of freight revenue with transborder (32%), overseas (35%) and U.S. domestic (16%) making up the rest, so a share below 1 is required. Overseas traffic (grain, potash, coal through Canadian ports) and Canadian-origin transborder traffic do enter StatCan's Canada total, which keeps the share fairly high; U.S. domestic movements do not. Revenue shares are used only to orient the tonnage share, which is why the band is wide.
assumptions.applies_when: p38's geographic scope is broader than StatCan's Canada total and the overlap can be captured by a single share in this band.
assumptions.falsified_by: Documentation that p38 is already exactly the Canada-only traffic StatCan counts, or a CN/CPKC disclosure allowing a direct Canada-only RTM split.

assumptions.name: July 2026 versus July 2025 intermodal unit growth factor
assumptions.rationale: p30/p31/p32 show July units of 195k, 192k and 208k in 2023-2025, so July 2025 rose on July 2024; p74 shows 2025 intermodal tonnage at an all-time high and p1 reports intermodal carloads still increasing in week 32 of 2026. Modest further growth is the central case, with a decline possible if tariffs or port conditions bite.
assumptions.applies_when: Intermodal demand continues along the 2025-2026 growth path through July 2026.
assumptions.falsified_by: Falling intermodal unit counts or port container throughput in mid-2026.

assumptions.name: Ratio of shortline and other non-Class-1 carrier tonnage to Canada-covered Class 1 tonnage, July 2026
assumptions.rationale: StatCan's total traffic carried covers all federal railways, while p38 covers only CN and CPKC. Canadian shortlines and regional/other carriers (e.g. Ontario Northland, G&W Canada properties, regional forest-product and potash feeders) are small relative to the two Class 1s, and much of their line-haul traffic is bridged onward and counted once in StatCan's series; a low single-digit percentage addition is therefore appropriate, with the upper band allowing a larger shortline share after grain and forest-product feeder movements. This is an allowance ratio, not a level of the target.
assumptions.applies_when: StatCan's 'all railways' coverage exceeds CN plus CPKC by shortlines and other reporting carriers of roughly this relative size in July 2026.
assumptions.falsified_by: StatCan documentation or carrier data showing non-Class-1 carriers account for more than about a tenth of Canadian rail tonnage.

The best estimate for total freight carried by Canadian railways in Canada during July 2026 is [[estimate]] [[unit]] ([[interval_level]] interval [[p10]] to [[p90]] [[unit]]). This targets StatCan's total traffic carried series, first release.

The anchor is [[p53_value]], the exact July 2024 total. Methods rebuild it three ways: a direct drift factor ([[a1_value]]), a channel sum of non-intermodal [[p59_value]], intermodal [[p55_value]] and US-origin [[p57_value]] traffic scaled by [[a2_value]], [[a3_value]] and [[a4_value]], and a Class [n] RTM route from [[p38_value]] with haul, share and shortline assumptions. Intermodal units [[p30_value]] and [[p31_value]] support a fourth cross-check. Only the July 2024 points are observed; every 2026 factor is an assumption. Code weighted the methods equally because backtest years were too few to calibrate errors, so the interval reflects input uncertainty only.

The main risk is a definition break or a July 2026-specific shock. A published July 2025 total would most improve the estimate.

The best estimate for total freight carried by Canadian railways in Canada during July 2026 is 29,472,905 t (80% model-based interval 15,641,780 to 55,534,098 t). This targets StatCan's total traffic carried series, first release.

The anchor is 29,900,000 metric tonnes, the exact July 2024 total. Methods rebuild it three ways: a direct drift factor (1.02), a channel sum of non-intermodal 23,200,000 metric tonnes, intermodal 2,800,000 metric tonnes and US-origin 3,800,000 metric tonnes traffic scaled by 1.01, 1.12 and 0.86, and a Class [n] RTM route from 111,388,000,000 revenue ton-miles with haul, share and shortline assumptions. Intermodal units 208,000 intermodal units and 192,000 intermodal units support a fourth cross-check. Only the July 2024 points are observed; every 2026 factor is an assumption. Code weighted the methods equally because backtest years were too few to calibrate errors, so the interval reflects input uncertainty only.

The main risk is a definition break or a July 2026-specific shock. A published July 2025 total would most improve the estimate.

- a2 July 2026 versus July 2024 non-intermodal tonnage factor: 1.01 dimensionless, range 0.7119 to 1.424 (range widened by code); used by m2, m4. Overturned by: Commodity-level evidence of a sharp 2026 fall in grain, potash, coal, iron ore or metals loadings relative to 2024.
- a3 July 2026 versus July 2024 intermodal tonnage factor: 1.12 dimensionless, range 0.7937 to 1.587 (range widened by code); used by m2. Overturned by: Falling intermodal unit counts in mid-2026, a port labour disruption, or evidence that 2026 intermodal volumes fell below 2025.
- a4 July 2026 versus July 2024 US-origin tonnage factor: 0.86 dimensionless, range 0.5916 to 1.183 (range widened by code); used by m2, m4. Overturned by: A rebound in US-origin traffic, or a Q3 2026 share back above roughly [n].
- a6 Average length of haul for the traffic represented by p38: 1,050 miles, range 757 to 1,515 (range widened by code); used by m3. Overturned by: A published Canada-specific average length of haul outside this range for Class [n] traffic.
- a7 July 2026 versus Q3 2025 monthly-average Class [n] tonnage factor: 1.02 dimensionless, range 0.721 to 1.442 (range widened by code); used by m3. Overturned by: A sharp month-specific change in 2026 RTMs relative to the year-to-date pattern, or a July-specific disruption.

by_construction: Only URLs leave the searcher (code regex); extractor, judge and final prompts never contain search result titles, snippets or the searcher's text. This holds by construction and is not measured.
residual_risks: The searcher sees post-cutoff search results and chooses which URLs are fetched, so page selection can be conditioned on the answer; only the URLs leave the searcher, and in backtests every fetched page is a snapshot dated <= as_of.
Live pages are used only when as_of is today; in backtests every page is an archived snapshot dated <= as_of.
The leak sentinel only catches registered official values in common formats, not paraphrased or derived numbers.
The model's own training data (knowledge cutoff unpublished) can include history before as_of; it cannot include the target if the target was published after the model's release.
Wayback snapshots are captured by a third party; a snapshot date <= as_of proves the content existed by then.
Assumption values are proposed by the judge model from its own knowledge, which can include the target's history before as_of; code checks their form, not where the number came from.
